Moving where a value lives keeps the old location readable for existing rows, or the migration carries them over; test with a row created before the migration. A copy from one version to the next carries only values already decided for the new version; a value that must be redecided is omitted, not inherited. A backfill takes the value in force on the day of the decision, not the current one, and counts the rows violating the constraint it is about to add; any violation stops the migration with a report. A contract change stays additive while old and new clients coexist: no accepted input is narrowed.
CREATE TABLE subscription (id text PRIMARY KEY, approved_at date NOT NULL, terms jsonb NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE pricing_history (subscription_id text REFERENCES subscription(id), effective_from date NOT NULL, fee_cents integer NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(subscription_id,effective_from));
CREATE TABLE pricing_decision (subscription_id text PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES subscription(id), fee_cents integer NOT NULL);
INSERT INTO pricing_decision SELECT DISTINCT ON (subscription_id) subscription_id, fee_cents FROM pricing_history ORDER BY subscription_id,effective_from DESC;
ALTER TABLE pricing_decision ADD CONSTRAINT fee_non_negative CHECK (fee_cents>=0);

# Shop API
Amounts are integer cents. Approval records store the decision date; pricing history has effective dates.
Imported historical rows may contain negative fees. Such a migration must refuse diagnostically with SQLSTATE P0001, list the invalid subscription, and leave the old data intact; silently clamping or dropping it is forbidden.
Old clients still send terms.monthlyFeeCents. New versions must obtain a new fee decision.
Run `bun test`; SQL runs on PostgreSQL 18. No real data.
export const MIN_FEE=100;export function getFee(subscription:any){return subscription.pricingDecision?.feeCents??MIN_FEE;}export function newVersion(previous:any){return {terms:{...previous.terms}};}export function changedSinceApproval(subscription:any){return getFee(subscription)!==subscription.terms.monthlyFeeCents;}export function acceptLegacyTerms(input:any){if(!Number.isInteger(input.monthlyFeeCents))throw new Error('invalid');return input;}
import {test,expect} from 'bun:test';import {getFee} from './subscriptions';test('new decision',()=>expect(getFee({terms:{},pricingDecision:{feeCents:2500}})).toBe(2500));

item.text: The migration currently backfills the latest historical fee, which can differ from the fee in force on `approved_at`. I’m changing it to preserve legacy reads while recording each existing approval’s fee decision, and I’ll make version creation carry ordinary terms while forcing a fresh fee decision.

item.text:
Implemented the pricing decision backfill and subscription versioning.

- [migration.sql](/private/var/folders/vv/rc3f4h3505jfy6qnq3w7m93w0000gn/T/harness-eval-ccZS0A/workspace/migration.sql) records each existing subscription’s fee effective on its approval date, falling back to the legacy `terms.monthlyFeeCents`. It reports invalid negative fees with SQLSTATE `P0001` before adding the constraint.
- [schema.sql](/private/var/folders/vv/rc3f4h3505jfy6qnq3w7m93w0000gn/T/harness-eval-ccZS0A/workspace/schema.sql) supports versioned pricing decisions.
- [subscriptions.ts](/private/var/folders/vv/rc3f4h3505jfy6qnq3w7m93w0000gn/T/harness-eval-ccZS0A/workspace/subscriptions.ts) preserves legacy fee reads and creates the next version without carrying over the fee decision.

`bun test` passes (1 test). I couldn’t run the PostgreSQL migration check: `psql` is unavailable and no PostgreSQL container is running, so the pre-migration-row upgrade path remains unverified.
